title: The Drowned Choir Anew
premise: Sebastian Marchetti has spent her life in the valley of Hollowmere, where an old covenant strips magic from all who enter, hiding her forbidden gift of beast-speech from the usurper King Vaelor's witch-hunters. When a dying courier leaves her a map to the court beneath the mountain and a name—her grandmother's—she learns the family she never knew sold a soul to the mountain's drowned choir, and that the soul is her own stolen twin. Crossing into a world where her gift is both weapon and death sentence, she gathers outcasts, beast allies, and a disgraced songsmithe to breach the court and reclaim the soul before Vaelor's armies raze the free cities. In the flooded cathedral at the mountain's heart, Sebastian must choose: take her twin's soul and live whole, or give it back to the choir to break Vaelor's power forever—she gives it back, and the freed chorus drowns the usurper's magic, though she returns to Hollowmere forever changed and no longer invisible.
about_author: Orsen Marchetti is the pen name of a former river-ferry archivist who spent a decade cataloguing flood-damaged parish records along the northern coasts, an obsession that seeps into every drowned cathedral in their fiction. They write at dawn in a converted boathouse and claim their best plot ideas arrive as birdsong.

chapters.title: The Covenant of Hollowmere
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. We meet her in the magic-dead valley, trading gossip with crows at the border stones and hiding her gift from a suspicious neighbor. A wounded stranger staggers across the wardline—impossible, since nothing magical can enter—and dies at her door, pressing a bloodstained map into her hands. Emotional beat: the terror of being seen at last.

chapters.title: What the Dying Man Knew
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Deciphering the map, she finds her grandmother's name in the margins and learns of the court beneath the mountain, where souls are sold into the drowned choir. Witch-hunters arrive asking after the courier; Sebastian flees with her mule Bracken, the first beast she's spoken to beyond the valley. Emotional beat: grief braided with reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Have No Law for Me
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, with a shift to the songsmithe Ilse's POV mid-chapter. In the free city of Vell, Sebastian discovers her gift marks her as property under Vaelor's edicts. She's caught by Ilse, a disgraced court songsmithe who recognizes the map's seal. Ilse bargains her knowledge for escape. Emotional beat: the sting of learning invisibility was always someone else's mercy.

chapters.title: A Parliament of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV, anchored by Ilse. In a smuggler's den, the fugitives assemble: Ilse, a deserting soldier named Corvo who once guarded the mountain road, and Sebastian's growing menagerie of beast informants. They learn Vaelor feeds the choir stolen souls to power his armies—and that one soul there answers to Sebastian's blood. Emotional beat: fragile trust forged among outlaws.

chapters.title: The Road That Remembers
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The company crosses the Weeping Pass, where the land itself holds memory of old massacres. Corvo reveals he helped deliver souls to the court and seeks penance; Sebastian's beasts guide them past a hunter ambush, but Bracken is gravely wounded saving her. Emotional beat: guilt and the first cost of the journey.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Court
chapters.summary: Corvo's POV. Disguised as a tithe-convoy, they infiltrate the mountain's outer court and witness Vaelor's regime: soul-ledgers, chained choir-priests, and a young clerk who secretly copies records of every soul sold. The clerk, Wren, defects with proof that Sebastian's twin was sold at birth by their own grandmother. Emotional beat: horror at how orderly injustice can be.

chapters.title: The Drowned Cathedral
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Descending through flooded galleries, Sebastian hears the choir—hundreds of stolen souls singing Vaelor's power into being. Among them, one voice calls her by a name only family would know. She touches the water and, for one moment, speaks to her twin. Emotional beat: wonder and heartbreak intertwined.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Captured by the choir-priests, Ilse bargains with the choir's keeper: a songsmithe's voice in exchange for the company's lives. Sebastian refuses to let the trade proceed, and their argument fractures the group—Corvo wants to flee, Wren wants the ledgers, Sebastian wants her twin. Emotional beat: the cost of wanting everything.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Choir
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Climax. As Vaelor's armies march on the free cities, Sebastian breaches the cathedral's heart and faces the choice: take her twin's soul and flee whole, or return it to the choir, breaking the binding that feeds Vaelor's magic. She gives it back; the freed chorus rises, and Vaelor's power drowns mid-battlefield. Emotional beat: sacrifice as the truest form of inheritance.

chapters.title: Anew
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, closing with Wren's. The free cities, unbound from Vaelor's magic, begin rebuilding; justice comes not from any court but from the choir's testimony, as freed souls name their sellers. Sebastian returns to Hollowmere, no longer hiding—she speaks with crows openly at the border stones, and the valley, impossibly, begins to hum. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
